issue.title: task-link marks viewport CPU guard still flakes under the full plugin suite
issue.description: Proposed by bob-cli-rc.1 note #1. scripts/test-ledger-tools-task-link-marks-live.cjs test "a viewport-limited build over a 1,000-line note stays fast" failed at 26.9 ms CPU in that phase full npm test and passed on its unchanged clean-base focused rerun. Landing on clean bob-plugins dca84529 independently ran this file alongside snooze vectors: all 37 viewport-file tests pass (57/58 combined, only the separately owned q5 snooze vector fails). This is distinct from bob-cli-pg taskLinks API p95 and bob-cli-f8 task-wikilink index/ranking budgets. Closed epic bob-cli-f5 note #3 already replaced wall-clock sampling with CPU warm-up and best-of samples; current lines 1176-1241 retain that mitigation. Investigate actual cost versus process-wide helper-thread/GC CPU contamination and preserve meaningful viewport and keystroke performance coverage; do not blindly raise budgets. Large because the precise cause of this post-mitigation recurrence is not established. No currently active epic causally owns this unchanged timing node.

task_type_fields.evidence: Phase bob-cli-rc.1 note #1: one full-suite miss at 26.9 ms CPU, followed by a passing focused clean-base rerun. Lander control at dca84529: 37/37 tests in this file pass. The lander did not independently reproduce the failure or establish an overall fail rate; the phase reports the fail/pass pair. Existing CPU warm-up and best-of sampling are present.
